label: first input token is one of {b,d,g,h,i,j,k,l,p,r,s,t,u,y,2,3}
explanation: Sequence-onset token detector. At step 0 the unit fires deterministically (precision 1.0) whenever the first original token is in a fixed set of 16 tokens {b,d,g,h,i,j,k,l,p,r,s,t,u,y,2,3}, and never fires at step 0 for the other 14 tokens (a,c,e,f,m,n,o,q,v,w,x,z,0,1). Magnitude is set by token identity: 2 is strongest (max), then p (~0.8), g (~0.7), with t, i, 3 also high; b (~0.24), d (~0.15), k (~0.13), l (~0.02) are weak. About 13% of activations (7% of mass) are weaker echoes at step 1 (and rarely step 2), mostly when the step-0 token was a strong one (e.g. 2 then 2 gives ~0.5). It never fires at step 3 or later, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase.

issues: Every factual claim held up. On test, the predicate has precision 1.0, recall 0.868, F1 0.929 and mass recall 0.929. It never fires at step 0 for the 14 excluded tokens (precision 0 over 46,644 steps). There are no activations at t>=3, on the delimiter or in the copy phase. Step 0 holds 92.9% of the activation mass, step 1 7.0% and step 2 0.1%.

The misses are one systematic class, all at step 1 (8,104 test steps, 7.1% of the mass). The explanation describes this class correctly but the predicate leaves it out. It is predictable: the step-1 token is one of the strong tokens {2,t,p,i,g} and the first token is also strong (one of 2,t,p,i,g,r,y,3). That clause alone has precision about 0.70 at step 1. If the first token is outside the 16-token set, step 1 almost never fires (precision 0.01).

Adding this step-1 clause raises test F1 from 0.929 to 0.966 and mass recall from 0.929 to 0.975, with precision 0.997. The original predicate is still a fair and honest summary, so the gap is small and the label is not refuted.
